content: Government publicly aimed to complete demilitarisation by 2018 and disengage the military from commercial activities.
Military commercial and civilian activities continued after that commitment.
Post-war military activities included farms, tourism, shops, eateries and hotels in the north and east.
Pannai, Mukamalai, Mandaithivu and Eluthumadduval checkpoints were reported reinstalled in January 2025 after earlier removals.
2026 official proceedings continue to treat civilian land release and resettlement in north/east as unresolved policy business.
Field intake reports a Rs 8.47m construction-cost recovery condition on Kilinochchi temple-land release.
verification_target: primary government/parliamentary record for amount and mechanism

content: Field intake reports partial land returns in 2025 and 2026, preventing a flat 'nothing moves' narrative.
Sinhala-nationalist sources frame northern camp reduction as sovereignty loss and strategic exposure to India.
Travel blog describes a 9.5 km loop, about 3-4 hours, with World's End first before mist develops.
World's End drop circulates as 880 m and 1,200 m; UNESCO nomination instead says nearly 1,000 m.
verification_target: Survey Department elevations and defined endpoints

content: Horton Plains lies above 2,000 m and combines montane forest and grassland with high endemism.
Horton Plains National Park is one component of the Central Highlands World Heritage property.
Horton Plains contributes headwaters to major river systems, making conservation a water-security instrument.
Field intake says Horton Plains uniquely permits hiking without a ranger and lacks a cliff barrier.
Baker's Falls toponym links the site to Samuel Baker and colonial highland recreation/hunting history.
